results.experiment: Exp 44 — benchmark variance across 5 diverse texts

verdict: TEXT-SENSITIVE with honest labeling: spectral wins on 3/5 texts (technical +4.4x, code +3.6x, prose +1.03x) but LOSES on 2/5 (conversational 0.86x, mixed 0.84x). The advantage is domain-dependent: strong on structured text (technical, code), weak on natural conversation. This is consistent with the mechanism: the key-gram collapse is more severe on redundant text, and technical/code text has MORE redundancy in its keys (more specialized vocabulary = more distinct key directions = more diffuse heads to prune). On conversational text the keys are more diverse and the spectral signal is weaker.
honest_label: The benchmark result from Exp 42 (5-10% pruning, single diverse text) was favorable. Across 5 text types at 10% pruning, spectral beats random on 3/5 with mean ratio 2.14±1.53. The variance is HIGH — the method is not universally better than random. Its sweet spot is structured/technical text. This must be stated in the paper.
